title: Private Deploy Kitchen-Sink Shiftlog Apr 2025
summary: Shiftlog covering the week of 2025-04-14: mixed onprem/VPC installs, three customer blockers, two network workarounds implemented, and next-step rollouts for field handoffs.
body:
Purpose
This is a working shiftlog for the Private Deploy team covering the hands-on install and handoff cadence for the week starting 2025-04-14. It is intentionally informal — notes from standups, quick triage writeups, temporary workarounds, and action items.

Attendees (regulars)
- Aisha Patel (owner, install lead)
- Diego Martinez (networking)
- Claire Nguyen (onprem runtime)
- Ravi Shah (security & compliance)
- Marta Ruiz (customer success handoff)
- rotating field engineers: Kevin L., Priya S., Omar Y.

Daily standup highlights (concise)
2025-04-14 (Mon)
- Kevin: completed initial node provisioning for Customer: Nimbly (E0). Ran into nvlink driver mismatch on the host image. Reverted to 535.18 kernel; temp fix.
- Diego: observed intermittent packet-loss on Site B during live install. Likely MTU mismatch between customer switch and our veth config. Setting MTU to 9000 on tunnel endpoints as a mitigation.
- Claire: discovered L0 compile warnings from the custom kernel module; not blocking but adds noise to logs. Filed JIRA-PLAT-8742.
- Action: Ravi to confirm KMS access with Nimbly before key rotation window on Thu.

2025-04-15 (Tue)
- Priya: onprem deploy at Acadia — installer completed but userland service intermittently crashes after warmstart. Tracepoints point to shared memory race when restoring KV cache.
- Claire: pushed a hotfix branch that adds a 250ms jitter to restore sequence; reduced crashes in staging. PR: github.com/redwood-inference/private-deploy/PR#341.
- Diego: firewall rules at Acadia require outbound DNS to a proxy (corporate policy). Worked with customer netsec to allow 8.8.8.8 egress and annotated runbook.
- Customer ask: Acadia wants a follow-up run to validate multi-AZ failover under traffic.

2025-04-16 (Wed)
- Omar: VPC demo for BetaOne — latency SLO met but token-level spikes during batching when bursts arrive. Observed that our batching window default (10ms) misses low-latency calls from BetaOne SDK.
- Action: experiment with adaptive batching for customers flagged as low-latency (A/B with factor 0.5ms window).
- Ravi: compliance checklist for Zenith (onprem, regulated) delayed by customer SOC team; placed a hold on day-2 logging changes until SOC sign-off.

Triage notes (deeper dives)
1) Nimbly nvlink/driver mismatch
- Symptom: GPUs not visible to runtime after kernel upgrade to 6.x; install fails at device discover.
- Root cause hypothesis: Customer base image had a newer kernel where our prebuilt driver binary doesn't match.
- Temporary workaround: revert host kernel to 5.15 + vendor driver 535.18. Documented in runbook under section "GPU-driver fallbacks".
- Permanent: task to add dynamic driver build in bootstrap (PLAT-8779). ETA: sprint 44.

2) Acadia shared-memory KV race
- Symptom: userland service crash on warmstart 10–30s after node is provisioned.
- Investigation: logs show concurrent restore threads touching the same mmap offset. Reproducer: init sequence with 12 concurrent allocations in dev.
- Mitigation: hotfix adds ordering and backoff; observed 94% reduction in crash rate in staging.
- Next: add a unit test and integrate into preflight check. Owner: Claire. Ticket: PLAT-8788.

3) BetaOne batching latency spikes
- Symptom: occasional 70ms bursts on otherwise <25ms p95. Correlates with traffic burst windows where many small requests arrive nearly simultaneously.
- Hypothesis: batching buffer waits for threshold or timeout; bursts coalesce and cause token-level jitter.
- Short-term: lower batching window for BetaOne by 80% and enable strict priority for low-latency routes.
- Long-term: implement adaptive windowing (feedback-based). Owner: Diego + runtime team.

Customer-facing escalations and notes
- Zenith (regulated onprem): SOC requested HDD-level encryption verification and HSM integration details. Ravi is the lead for SOC contact. Status: awaiting SOC PO approval (expected 4/21).
- Acadia: wants multi-AZ failover stress test; sequencing required with their infra team — Marta to schedule for week of 4/28.
- Nimbly: driver rollback accepted; customer requested a post-install remediation plan. Propose a maintenance window 4/20 for kernel-driver reconciliation.

Workarounds applied this week (operational)
- MTU tunnel adjustment to 9000 on site B for Nimbly; documented on runbook and network diagram updated.
- Added DNS egress allowance for Acadia to permit NTP and external resolver (temporary proxy exception).
- Hotfix branch for KV restore ordering pushed to staging and smoke-tested on two nodes.

Open risks and blockers
- Driver dynamic-build (PLAT-8779) is medium risk; without it installs for customers who run newer kernels will remain manual. Risk impact: medium (install velocity).
- SOC sign-off delay for Zenith blocks day-2 logging changes; could delay go-live by up to 2 weeks. Mitigation: provide a focused compliance packet and schedule a mini-audit.
- Field bandwidth: two field engineers on PTO next week (Kevin, Priya) — may require shifting scheduled installs or bringing on contractor support.

Decisions made this week
- Agree to run targeted adaptive batching experiments for two customers (BetaOne + internalCanary). If p95 improves, roll adaptive batching as opt-in for latency-sensitive customers.
- Accept driver rollback for Nimbly and schedule a reconciliation maintenance window 4/20.
- Freeze day-2 logging changes for Zenith until SOC completes the requested evidence collection.

Action items (owners and ETA)
- Claire: add unit test for KV restore ordering and merge to mainline. ETA: 2025-04-21.
- Diego: implement adaptive-batching prototype and run A/B with BetaOne. ETA: 2025-04-24.
- Ravi: prepare compliance evidence packet for Zenith (HSM, KMS, disk encryption details). ETA: 2025-04-18.
- Marta: schedule Acadia multi-AZ failover stress window with their infra team. ETA: 2025-04-22.
- Aisha: coordinate Nimbly maintenance window and ensure on-call coverage during rollback. ETA: 2025-04-20.
- Ops (rotating): update runbook pages (GPU-driver fallbacks, MTU troubleshooting, DNS proxy exceptions). ETA: 2025-04-17.

Notes to self / runbook fragments to copy into Confluence
- "Driver fallback flow": steps to detect kernel mismatch, probe with lspci/nvidia-smi, automated rollback script snippet, manual escalation checklist.
- "KV warmstart checklist": preflight memory checks, single-threaded restore toggle, smoke-test list.
- "Adaptive batching experiment": traffic tagging, metric set (p50/p95/p99 token latency and tail QPS), rollback criteria.

Misc (quick mentions)
- Small ops improvement: added a check to the install script that detects corporate proxies and surfaces DNS egress failure early. Saves ~30m on some installs.
- Cross-team ask: ask Observability to add a per-deployment label for kernel-version in traces; will help triage future driver mismatches.

Summary and next sync
We had a noisy week but closed off a couple of practical mitigations (KV hotfix, MTU workaround, DNS exception) that stabilized two active installs. Major outstanding work is driver dynamic-build and SOC evidence for Zenith. Next sync: ad-hoc triage on Fri 2025-04-18 10:30 PT to review BetaOne A/B results and confirm Nimbly maintenance slot.

If you see anything missing or want to add a quick note, append to this doc — this is a living log and meant to be copied into the more formal runbooks once stabilized.

End of log.
